title: The Influence of glycemic control on periodontal parameters in type II diabetics
summary: The chronic diseases periodontitis and diabetes mellitus type 2 are considered common diseases due to their high prevalences and influence each other.  The study investigates the question to what extent medication-based blood glucose control influences the health of the gums. While it is known that elevated blood glucose levels lead to inflammation of the gums, it is currently unknown whether controlling blood glucose with medication also leads to a reduction in inflammation of the gums. In the planned study, the effects of blood glucose control on periodontal status will be investigated in 50 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus. For this purpose, voluntary patients who present themselves for the first time at the Diabetology Outpatient Clinic of the University Hospital of Freiburg will undergo dental examinations (measurement of pocket depths, recessions, degree of inflammation, loosening of the teeth and presence of plaque) before and after blood glucose control. The dental examinations take place at 3-month intervals.

interventions.name: At T1 (baseline), blood glucose control is started in the Department of Endocrinology & Diabetology, and periodontal status and oral hygiene and gingival indices (BOP, GI, PI) are recorded in the Department of Operative Dentistry and Periodontology (max. one week). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with chronically elevated long-term blood glucose levels, diabetes mellitus type 2 HbA1c ≥ 8 %, periodontitis stage I-IV
Exclusion criteria:
Patients requiring acute treatment (e.g. periodontal abscess) or undergoing active dental treatment (e.g. periodontal therapy), smokers, severe general diseases (tumor diseases, palliative therapies), cortisone therapy, antibiotic therapy up to 6 months before study participation, pregnancy, and breastfeeding.
